neighbours.label: the end of a fronted perspective phrase 'For <person>,' / 'Pour <person>,' / 'Для <person>' that says from whose point of view the clause holds
fire: The job paid well. For my brother, though, the long hours were too much.
Most guests enjoyed the soup. For the children, it was far too spicy.
The rules changed last year. For small farmers, this meant higher costs.
Il a beaucoup plu. Pour nous, les vacances étaient quand même belles.
The exam was postponed. For many students, the delay was a relief.
Paris was crowded. For my parents, the trip was still a dream come true.
The film got mixed reviews. For me, it was the best of the year.
Prices rose again. For retired people, every euro now counts.
quiet: The job paid well. In the winter, though, the long hours were too much.
Most guests enjoyed the soup. On the second night, it was far too spicy.
The rules changed last year. In most regions, this meant higher costs.
Il a beaucoup plu. En juillet, les vacances étaient quand même belles.
The exam was postponed. By Friday morning, the delay was official.
Paris was crowded. In the end, the trip was still a dream come true.
The film got mixed reviews. At the festival, it was shown twice.
Prices rose again. Since January, every euro now counts.

notes: Card peaks: comma after 'pour moi', 'for Egypt', 'Pour elle'; 'Для вас' x3; ' whom' x4. Probe: 'For her,' 0.45 vs 'After lunch,' 0.01. Near misses keep a fronted phrase but of time/place, not a person's perspective.
